finding: sas_round / sas_round_scalar (:133) use floor(|x|+0.5) with no fuzz. SAS ROUND rounds a value that is APPROXIMATELY halfway away from zero (it fuzzes to match decimal arithmetic; ROUNDZ is the unfuzzed variant). Repro: sas_round(2.4999999999999996) = 2.0 and sas_round(-2.4999999999999996) = -2.0 (SAS: 3 / -3; such values arise from 600 + 250*(1-pd) float noise). Also wrong for |x| >= 2^52: sas_round(4503599627370497.0) = 4503599627370498.0 because x+0.5 rounds to even before floor (SAS returns the integer unchanged). sas_round(-0.4) returns -0.0. The check script tests only exact .5 ties (2.5, -2.5, 0.5, -0.5).
cites: RULEBOOK §2 round(x) row (half away from zero); inventory train.sas credit_risk_score row and predict.sas credit_risk_score / risk_grade row (sas_compat.sas_round); SAS ROUND / ROUNDE / ROUNDZ documentation (ROUND fuzzes approximately-halfway values)
fix: Return x unchanged when |x| >= 2**52. Otherwise round half away from zero from the 15-significant-digit decimal form (Decimal(f'{x:.14e}').quantize(1, ROUND_HALF_UP), the same A18 machinery as _fixed) so 2.4999999999999996 -> 3. Add 0.0 to drop -0.0. Mark the fuzz width TODO(port) (SAS's exact tolerance is undocumented). Use the same code for sas_round_scalar.

finding: input_best32 returns +inf, which is neither SAS missing nor null, for overflowing numeric text: input('1E400') -> inf. SAS gives missing plus an invalid-data note. This contradicts the docstring ('anything else -> missing') and the module convention (missing = null). It also parses the whole string, but best32. reads only the first 32 columns: a 35-digit string gives 1.23e34 where SAS reads 32 digits (1.23e31). '1e5', ' 12 ', '-', '.', '+5' and '-.5' all match SAS (checked).
cites: RULEBOOK §2 input(s, best32.) row ('numeric text -> float, anything else -> missing'); §2 numeric missing row (null, never NaN or inf); inventory feature_engineering.sas / predict.sas MonthlyIncome_num rows
fix: After the cast, add .then(v).when(~v.is_finite()) -> None, i.e. pl.when(t matches & v.is_finite()).then(v). Apply s.str.slice(0, 32) before strip_chars to mirror the 32-column informat width, and mark the width rule TODO(port) (unverified).

finding: Output names differ from the polars expressions the helpers replace. div(pl.col('lift'), k) is named 'a' (the struct's first field), sas_sum(...) and lt(...) are named 'literal', while plain polars keeps 'lift'. A translation that writes df.with_columns(sas_compat.div(pl.col('x'), n)) without .alias silently ADDS a column 'a' and leaves x undivided. That changes judged columns and values. Also, div inside group_by().agg returns list[f64] ([0.5]) where the plain polars quotient returns f64 (map_batches is not marked as returning a scalar). The check script always aliases and never uses agg.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 arithmetic row (div is mandatory for every scalar/aggregate divisor, so it replaces `a / b` everywhere); §2 sum / comparison rows; §0 structure-preserving (same columns)
fix: End each Expr helper with .alias(_e(first_arg).meta.output_name(raise_if_undetermined=False) or ...), or state in the module docstring 'always .alias() the result; never call div inside agg'. Pass returns_scalar=True when both operands are aggregates, or raise in that case.

finding: sas_best applies the E-notation threshold 0 < |x| < 1e-5 at EVERY width. A15 calibrated that threshold only for BEST12. (reference cells), but sas_best(x, 8) is the A9 INTO helper and the function is public for any w. At small widths it prints a nonzero value as '0': sas_best(1.5e-5, 6) = '0', sas_best(-1.5e-5, 8) = '-0.00002' (1 significant digit). It also exceeds the width: sas_best(-1e-6, 4) = '-1E-6' (5 chars), sas_best(-100, 3) = '-1E2'. BEST never prints 0 for a nonzero value. No TODO(port) marks the unverified widths (UNKNOWN rule). The check script tests width 8 only at 0.0667, 1/3 and integers.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 PROC EXPORT row (A15: E below 1e-5 is a BEST12. rule); §2 select into row (A9: BEST8.); §2 UNKNOWN rule; experiment X03 covers only 0.0667, 1/3, 7000, 123456789
fix: Restrict sas_best to w in {8, 12} (assert) and add 'TODO(port): E-notation threshold verified only at w=12 (A15); BEST8. below 1e-4 unverified'. Or run an X03-style experiment for BEST8. on 1.5e-5 and 9.9e-6 and encode the result.

finding: fmt_wd returns text WIDER than w when the integer part does not fit. fmt_wd(123456789, 8, 4) = '123456789' (9 chars), fmt_wd(1e10, 8, 2) = '10000000000'. SAS w.d falls back to BESTw. ('1.2346E8') and logs 'NOTE: At least one W.D format was too small for the number to be printed'. This contradicts the docstring ('SAS keeps the width'). sas_d8 (:250) and sas_d12_3 have the same overflow: sas_d8(123456789) = '123456789', sas_d12_3(1e12) = '1000000000000' (13 > 12).
cites: RULEBOOK §2 PROC EXPORT row (A24: w.d keeps width w); SAS w.d format documentation (shifts to BESTw. when the value does not fit); inventory metrics_calculation.sas decile_analysis.csv row (8.4/8.2) and train.sas model_summary.csv row (8.4)
fix: After the decimal-dropping loop, return sas_best(x, w) when len(s) > w. Do the same in sas_d8 (BEST8.) and sas_d12_3 (BEST12.).

finding: fmt_percent prints negatives with a minus sign: fmt_percent(-0.05, 8, 2) = '-5.00%', fmt_percent(-1.0, 8, 2) = '-100%'. SAS PERCENTw.d encloses negative values in PARENTHESES ('(5.00%)'; PERCENTNw.d is the minus-sign variant). The width reservation the docstring describes ('reserves two positions') is exactly the room for those parentheses, so the code knows the rule but does not apply it. Values above 999% also overflow w: fmt_percent(1000, 8, 2) = '100000%'. All judged percent8.2 columns are >= 0 today.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 PROC EXPORT row (A14/A24 percentw.d); SAS PERCENTw.d format documentation ('encloses negative values in parentheses'); inventory risk_scores_train.csv, decile_analysis.csv and printed_cumulative_lift.csv rows
fix: When x < 0 and the rounded text is not zero, return '(' + _fixed(-v, dec) + '%)', using the same width loop with the limit w (parentheses included). Fall back to E-notation / BESTw. when no decimal count fits.

finding: write_sas_csv silently ignores a `formats` key that names no column, and _render_column (:337) returns String columns verbatim before looking at fmt. A misspelt key (formats={'Interest_rate': 'percent8.2'}), or a percent format on a column that proc_import_csv imported as text, therefore writes BEST12./raw text ('0.05' instead of '5.00%') with no error. Formatted columns are judged by compare.py FORMATTED.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 PROC EXPORT row and `format x ... attached to a column` row (formats= argument); inventory train.sas risk_scores_train.csv row (formats={'interest_rate': 'percent8.2'})
fix: Raise ValueError when a formats key is not in df.columns, or when a numeric format is given for a pl.String column.

finding: The rulebook maps `format x best12.` to 'the formats= argument at export time', but _render_column raises 'unsupported format' for 'best12.', 'BEST8.' and the no-decimal 'w.' form ('8.'), because _WD_RE needs digits after the point. A Boolean column also raises ValueError (float('True')). Text values are written verbatim, including trailing blanks that SAS's DSD export trims. cites: RULEBOOK §2 row '`format x best12.` / `format x 8.4` / percent8.2 / date9. attached to a column -> the formats= argument'

finding: fit_logistic divergence handling is wrong in four ways. (a) Complete separation (x=1..8, y=0000 1111) raises numpy LinAlgError 'Singular matrix'. SAS warns 'Complete separation of data points detected' and still reports estimates. (b) Quasi-complete separation (tie at x=5) returns converged=True with beta [-191.4, 38.3] and Wald chi-square 1e-12, because the Newton step underflows to exactly 0. No warning. (c) If 40 halvings (:422) never restore -2 Log L, the loop still applies the step with t=2^-40, and the convergence test on the DAMPED step max|t*step| < 1e-10 (:429) then reports converged=True, although the full Newton step is not small. (d) An all-zero response runs 100 iterations to beta -101 with converged=False, and stepwise_logistic never reads .converged. A collinear design also raises LinAlgError (stepwise pre-screens aliasing, but direct callers do not).
cites: RULEBOOK §2 model fitting row (A17: 'halving the step while -2 Log L increases, to full convergence (max abs step < 1e-10)'); SAS PROC LOGISTIC separation checks and MAXITER=25 default; inventory train.sas stepwise row
fix: Test convergence on the FULL Newton step (or relative gradient), never t*step. When the line search fails, stop with converged=False. Catch LinAlgError and detect separation (max pd within 1e-8 of 0/1 for every row / w underflow), returning converged=False plus a reason. Have stepwise_logistic raise or warn on an unconverged fit. Cite the 100-iteration cap (SAS default MAXITER=25).

The module still picks 100 iterations and 40 halvings, and returns silently, with no TODO(port) marker. cites: RULEBOOK §2 UNKNOWN rule ('mark TODO(port): with the open question'); §3 marker format; module docstring line 8

finding: P-values come from a hand-written chi-square tail (_sf1 erfc form; _chi2_sf closed form for HL df=8), not the sanctioned scipy.stats.chi2.sf, although scipy is a declared dependency (pyproject.toml). cites: RULEBOOK §1 Numerics row ('scipy only for scipy.stats.chi2.sf (p-values)'); §2 preamble ('an implementer who invents a second mapping for a listed construct is violating a rule')
